messages:
maria: Heads-up — weekend oncall + new shadowing. Need someone to primary Sat 00:00–12:00 UTC and a shadow for that shift. There's a 03:00–07:00 UTC coverage thin spot we should explicitly hand off for. Tagging @alex @sam for availability.

alex: I can take primary for Sat morning if that helps. can someone drop the runbook link here? i'm still catching up on the new pager flows.

maria: awesome — thanks alex. runbook + short checklist: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-handbook
- paging: page primary via PagerDuty -> if no ack in 5m escalate to secondary
- customer-impact triage: run the quick-impact script, post to #incidents as "impact-summary"
- escalation: page SRE lead verbally after 15m if page unresolved

maria: quick copy of the escalation command (for reference):
```
# escalate to oncall lead (internal tool)
redwood-escalate --team oncall --to lead --reason "unacked page / customer impact"
```

incident-bot: :rotating_light: TEST ALERT: paging flow test triggered by maria for verification. This is a test — do not escalate.

sam: I can be the shadow for alex. i'm new to oncall but available Sat. can we do a short runthrough before the shift? would like to see most common pages + quick playbook.

jeff: noting the thin spot — most pages between 03–05 UTC are infra noisy, historically flaky autoscaler alerts. we should preemptively suppress the low-signal alert group and ensure runbook steps for the autoscaler are refreshed.

maria: plan suggestion: alex primary 00:00–12:00 UTC, sam shadow/secondary. jeff do the 11:30 handoff for context (11:45 UTC overlap). decision: suppress autoscaler low-signal alerts 02:45–07:30 UTC and add a monitor check at 07:20 UTC to re-enable.

shadow-bot: assigned onboarding checklist to sam — items: read oncall playbook, run the quick-impact script locally, join 30m shadow session with jeff. Due: 2026-03-20.

sam: thanks! quick Q — for customer-impact assessment what's the minimum we should include in the incident post? i.e., who to ping on support and what fields to fill.

maria: short template — paste into the incident thread:
- impact: customers affected (count/segment)
- symptom: user-visible effect
- scope: % of traffic / endpoints impacted
- mitigation: what's done / rollback status
- next steps / owner
also ping @support-lead and @account-ops for high-severity customers.

alex: also — when shadowing, sam, watch for two common things: (1) KV-cache OOMs causing timeouts, (2) delayed tokenization pipeline causing spike in latency. Both have quick mitigations in runbook (cache clear, fall back to smaller batch).

jeff: i'll do a 30-min pairing session Fri 18:30 PT (Sat 01:30 UTC) to walk through the autoscaler play and common alerts. sam, sound good?

sam: yup that works for me. thanks jeff. will be there. :thumbsup:

maria: final notes for handoff protocol:
- handoff msg in channel at -15m with current alerts and any mitigations in flight
- primary should confirm ability to receive pages (phone + pd ack) before shift start
- if primary misses two PD retries, secondary gets paged and oncall lead notified
- document any post-shift follow-ups in the "oncall-handoffs" doc page

alex: i'll post the -15m handoff and do a quick systems check 10m prior. sam — i'll DM creds/access you for debug tools.

maria: perfect. thanks everyone. if anythin pages during the shadow session treat it as real and follow runbook (we'll mark incident as "shadow exercise" if it's non-prod).

sam: acknowledged — appreciate the clarity. excited to shadow.

jeff: noted, will update the autoscaler alert suppression schedule and leave a timestamped note in the runbook.

maria: closing plan — primary/secondary set, shadow scheduled, pairing session scheduled. i'll follow up with a calendar invite and the suppression window. :white_check_mark:
